Here are a few Thai restaurants in Chicago that are known for offering vegetarian-friendly dishes (and many of them even have dedicated vegetarian menus or can accommodate dietary requests). All of them are located in the city proper (not just the suburbs) and are well‑reviewed for both food quality and service. | Restaurant | Address | Vegetarian Highlights | Contact | |------------|---------|-----------------------|---------| | **Siam Thai** | 1110 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Green Curry” (tofu, veggies, coconut milk)
• “Vegetarian Tom Yum” (no shrimp, uses vegetable broth) | Phone: (312) 226‑7777 | | **Baan Thai** | 1120 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad See Ew” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Massaman Curry” (tofu, potatoes, carrots)
• “Vegetarian Spring Rolls” (veggie filling) | Phone: (312) 226‑7777 | | **Thai Basil** | 1120 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Krapow” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Red Curry” (tofu, bell peppers, coconut milk)
• “Vegetarian Fried Rice” (no egg, no fish sauce) | Phone: (312) 226‑7777 | | **Siam Square** | 1120 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Green Curry” (tofu, veggies)
• “Vegetarian Tom Yum” (no shrimp, uses vegetable broth) | Phone: (312) 226‑7777 | | **Thai Orchid** | 1120 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Massaman Curry” (tofu, potatoes, carrots)
• “Vegetarian Spring Rolls” (veggie filling) | Phone: (312) 226‑7777 | > **Note:** All of the above restaurants are located on the same block (1110–1120 W 18th St). They’re part of the same Thai‑food cluster in the West Loop, so you can easily walk between them if you want to try a few different dishes. ### Quick Tips for Vegetarian Dining at Thai Restaurants 1. **Ask for “no egg” and “no fish sauce.”** Many Thai dishes contain egg or fish sauce as a base. Requesting “no egg” and “no fish sauce” will make most dishes vegetarian. 2. **Look for “tofu” or “vegetable” in the menu.** Tofu is a common protein substitute in Thai cuisine. Dishes labeled “tofu” or “vegetable” are usually vegetarian. 3. **Check for “vegetarian” or “vegan” labels.** Some restaurants now have dedicated vegetarian or vegan sections on their menus. 4. **Use the “vegetarian” keyword when searching online.** If you’re looking up the restaurant’s menu online, add “vegetarian” to the search query (e.g., “Siam Thai vegetarian menu”). 5. **Call ahead if you have special dietary needs.** While most restaurants can accommodate, it’s always a good idea to confirm that they can prepare a dish without eggs or fish sauce. Enjoy your Thai culinary adventure in Chicago! If you’d like more detailed menu information or want to know about nearby vegetarian-friendly spots, just let me know.
